summary.headline: School Committee holds FY27 budget hearing, reviews audit and OPEB liability, and retires the junior post-prom party.
summary.summary: The Northborough-Southborough Regional School Committee held a public hearing on its proposed $31.4 million FY27 operating budget, which represents a 5.81 percent increase over FY26. The committee also accepted the FY25 financial audit, which had no findings, and discussed long-term funding strategies for its $48 million retiree health insurance liability. In other business, high school administration announced the retirement of the decades-old overnight Junior Post-Prom Party and provided an update on curriculum mapping and student stress.

topics.title: Public hearing on proposed FY27 operating budget
topics.summary: The committee opened and closed a public hearing on the proposed FY27 regional school operating budget. The proposed budget totals $31,416,287, representing an increase of 5.81 percent over FY26. No members of the public commented during the hearing.
key_details: Proposed FY27 operating budget totals $31,416,287, a 5.81 percent increase over FY26.
Regular day programs account for $26,037,470 of the budget.
Special education programs account for $5,378,817, offset by circuit breaker reimbursements.
The hearing received no public comments and was closed.
topics.outcome: Hearing closed; budget will go before Annual Town Meetings in Southborough and Northborough.
topics.why_it_matters: The regional school budget determines Northborough and Southborough town assessments and school operational funding for the upcoming school year.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee approved open meeting and executive session minutes from prior meetings, received the Competency Determination Policy J-400 for first distribution, and reviewed upcoming Town Meeting dates. The meeting was adjourned at 8:11 PM.
key_details: Approved open meeting minutes from February 25, 2026, and collective bargaining subcommittee minutes from January 15, 2026.
Distributed Policy J-400 (Competency Determination) for initial review.
Noted Southborough Town Meeting is set for April 11, 2026, and Northborough Town Meeting for April 27, 2026.
topics.outcome: Minutes approved; policy distributed; meeting adjourned.

topics.title: Legislative budget update
topics.summary: The superintendent provided a brief state legislative update. The district is awaiting state House and Senate budget proposals and noted that a supplemental budget bill filed in the House included Fair Share surtax surplus funds, which may support regional transportation and special education circuit breaker reimbursements up to 75 percent.
key_details: State representatives filed Fair Share amendments for regional transportation and special education.
Surplus surtax funds could potentially increase circuit breaker reimbursement from 61.36 percent to 75 percent.
topics.outcome: Informational update; no formal action taken.

topics.title: FY25 financial audit and OPEB liability review
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the FY25 financial audit report from Scanlon and Associates and an actuarial valuation of Other Post-Employment Benefits (OPEB). The independent auditor issued an unqualified opinion with no findings, but officials highlighted a long-term OPEB liability of more than $48 million, which leaves the district with a negative net financial position of approximately $16 million. Committee members discussed creating a 10-year plan to increase the district's annual OPEB trust contributions from the current $25,000 per year.
key_details: Scanlon and Associates issued an unmodified audit opinion with no findings.
Total OPEB liability exceeds $48 million, contributing to a negative net position of approximately $16 million.
District OPEB funding ratio is just over 1 percent, with annual trust contributions at $25,000.
The committee discussed implementing an incremental 10-year funding plan to reduce long-term unfunded liabilities.
topics.outcome: The committee voted unanimously to accept the FY25 financial audit report.
topics.why_it_matters: Unfunded retiree health liabilities affect long-term district finances and municipal balance sheets for Northborough and Southborough.

topics.title: Algonquin Regional High School library presentation
topics.summary: The high school librarian presented an overview of library programming, circulation trends, and collection management. The library holds 18,851 items, representing 13.9 items per student compared to the state recommendation of 20, partly due to a recent comprehensive weeding of outdated non-fiction. A partnership with the Northborough and Southborough public libraries helped restore access to Gale databases after state and federal budget cuts.
key_details: Collection contains 18,851 items, or 13.9 items per student (state guideline recommends 20).
45 percent of the collection is classified as diverse titles and 32 percent supports student wellbeing.
More than 36,000 student visits and 7,500 material circulations were recorded through March 6.
Partnership with town libraries preserved access to over 80 digital databases.

topics.title: Student advisory report, curriculum mapping, and post-prom party changes
topics.summary: The student representative reported on school activities, cafeteria food shortages during third lunch, and rising academic stress among students. The high school principal outlined progress on curriculum mapping, with all core curriculum maps scheduled for completion by June 2027 and elective maps by June 2028. Additionally, the principal announced that the parent-teacher organization has retired the overnight Junior Post-Prom Party after roughly 30 years due to declining student interest and late sign-ups, redirecting funds to enrich prom night directly.
key_details: Students reported popular food options running out by the third lunch shift; administration is investigating with cafeteria vendor Whitsons.
School Council is examining student stress, over-scheduling, and the potential benefits of study halls.
Core curriculum mapping is slated for full completion by June 2027, with a progress report to NEASC in May 2026.
The overnight Junior Post-Prom Party has been retired by the PTO, with funds redirected to prom events.
topics.outcome: Informational updates; no formal action taken.

topics.title: FY26 budget variances and revenue report
topics.summary: The committee approved three minor budget variances in the FY26 operating budget and reviewed the monthly revenue report. The general fund had $504,143 (1.7 percent) remaining at approximately the three-quarters mark of the fiscal year. Approved variances included $89.02 for assistant superintendent supplies, $2,081 for Section 504 tutoring, and $1,327 for postage meter replenishment.
key_details: Operating budget has $504,143 remaining, or 1.7 percent, on track with prior-year spending.
Approved variances: $89.02 for assistant superintendent supplies, $2,081 for teacher specialists (504 tutoring), and $1,327 for postage.
Revenue collection is tracking at approximately 75 percent, with three of four quarterly town assessment payments received.
topics.outcome: Approved budget variances and accepted the FY26 revenue report unanimously.
